A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

alpha2C-adrenergic receptor expression is increased in human cutaneous smooth muscle cells by a serum-stimulated increase in cAMP, which is mediated by COX-2-dependent release of prostaglanding, and that this response is mediated by Rap1, but not A-kinase, signaling.
alpha(2C)AR expression is regulated by cAMP signaling in human cutaneous vascular smooth muscle cells, and that this regulation involves a COX2-dependent mechanism and a cAMP/Rap1-mediated mechanism.

The main takeaway from our work is that

cAMP signaling in cutaneous Vascular Smooth Muscle Cells (VSMCs) has a biphasic effect on alpha2C-adrenergic receptor (alpha2C-AR) expression: activation of alpha2C-AR transcription via Rap GTPase and inhibition via A-kinase, with the former predominating in serum-stimulating VSMCs.
the cAMP pathway is complex and that different cAMP signaling pathways may have opposing effects on alpha(2C)AR gene expression.
the alpha(2)-AR subtypes are regulated by distinct cAMP signaling pathways in human cutaneous arteriolar VSMCs.
